headline: Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC says its quarterly revenue jumped 51% as demand for AI chips held up.
score_reason: Company's own monthly and quarterly revenue, confirmed by a second outlet; pool score 8 kept.
importance_line: It matters most to investors and to the companies that buy TSMC's chips, including Nvidia and Apple, though one quarter of sales cannot show how long AI orders will last.
summary: Startup Fortune reports that TSMC said its third-quarter revenue rose 51% from a year earlier to NT$1.49 trillion. The total beat the NT$1.46 trillion analysts expected, according to Bloomberg, which suggests demand for AI chips has held up for now.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (403); read on Startup Fortune, which cites Bloomberg for the analyst figure. Euronews confirms the 51% and NT$1.49 trillion. Dollar conversions differ between outlets, so none is printed.
